title: Check yourself: Diagnosing a weak output, and a template builder

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A prompt asks Claude to describe "our current pricing", and the reply lists plausible but wrong tiers. The team's first idea is a longer prompt with stronger wording. What is the best diagnosis?

options.text: The rate card never reached the request, so the answer is a guess
options.says: Content absent from the prompt is filled with a plausible guess, which is missing context plus a hallucination (the diagnosis table and its first illustrative case).

options.text: The wording lacks force, so a longer prompt with firmer phrasing will make the tiers right
options.says: Ruled out because "No wording makes a model know yesterday's news or add exactly", and by the same reasoning no wording supplies a rate card.

options.text: The wrong model is answering, so moving up one tier fixes it
options.says: Ruled out because the table reserves the wrong-model cause for "Correct instructions, correct context, still a capability or speed miss", and here the context is missing.

options.text: The format is unclear, so the reply needs an explicit table layout
options.says: Ruled out because the symptom is "Generic or invented content; the answer ignores facts only you know", which the table assigns to missing context, not format.

questions.stem: After a revision of a classification prompt, one ticket that used to fail now passes, but two that used to pass now fail. Four changes were made at once. What should the team do?

options.text: Keep all four, since the case that failed before now passes
options.says: Ruled out because "A fix that repairs one input and quietly breaks three others is a regression".

options.text: Add a fifth to cover the two new failures, then re-run the set
options.says: Ruled out because "Several simultaneous edits leave you unable to say what helped", and a fifth edit adds to them.

options.text: Revert, then reapply the edits singly, checking the whole set each time
options.says: One change at a time against a fixed set is the method, and a regression means the edits interact (the one-at-a-time section).

options.text: Switch to a larger model to absorb the interactions between the four
options.says: Ruled out because the method says "or switch the model. Not several", and a larger model adds yet another variable.
